processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Sound portion of the 30 kg vacuum-induction-melted ingot of the 28Mn5Ni alloy was homogenized at 1423 K for 2.5 h.
Hot rolled at 1323 K; final hot-rolled plate thickness ~13 mm. This condition is hereafter referred to as HR. Details of hot rolling reported elsewhere [21].

Hot-rolled plates were cold rolled at room temperature in several passes to ~50% reduction in thickness (~6 mm thick sheets); denoted HR+CR. 15Mn5Ni cracked beyond 50%, so reduction was restricted to 50% for all alloys.

Cold rolled sheet heat treated at 873 K for 1 h followed by water quenching; this specific 873 K condition defines the present sample. This is the lowest temperature of the 873-1273 K heat treatment range and is documented for hardness only.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Bulk Vickers hardness under a peak load of 30 kg (~300 N) with a dwell time of 15 s; values averaged over ten measurements on each sample.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Peak load 30 kg (~300 N), dwell time 15 s, per ASTM E-140-02; value averaged over ten measurements on the sample
characterization_methods.purpose: To evaluate the change in mechanical properties (hardness) of the cold rolled 28Mn5Ni alloy upon heat treatment in the range 873-1273 K
characterization_methods.key_findings: For the Ni-containing 28Mn5Ni alloy, heat treatment at 873 K after 50% cold reduction increased the bulk hardness to 500 VHN, the highest among the heat-treatment temperatures investigated.

unmapped_findings: The 873 K heat-treatment condition of the 28Mn5Ni alloy is documented for hardness only; EBSD/OIM, XRD and TEM microstructural characterization was performed at 973 K, 1023 K and 1173 K, so no microstructure (recrystallization fraction, grain size, B2/κ-carbide fraction) is reported specifically for this 873 K sample.

Upon subsequent heat treatment at 873 K after 50% cold reduction, the hardness of the Ni-containing 28Mn5Ni alloy was increased to 500 VHN, while the Ni-free 28Mn0Ni alloy showed no noticeable change in hardness at this temperature.

In Fig. 8b the ~873 K data point is the highest of the Ni-containing series (just below 500 VHN); error bars are shown for the 28Mn5Ni (red circle) series but no numeric uncertainty for the 873 K value is tabulated.

The paper attributes the variation in hardness of the LDS alloys as a function of heat treatment temperature to precipitation and dissolution of secondary phases (κ-carbides and B2 particles) together with recrystallization and grain growth phenomena, depending on alloy composition.

As context for this sample's precursor HR+CR state, all three alloys (including 28Mn5Ni) saturated at around 450 VHN at 50% cold reduction, and the HR-condition hardness of 28Mn5Ni was reported as ~268 +/- 5 VHN [21].
